title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 215 (Firm, body corporate or association not to be appointed as inspector)

content.overview: Section 215 provides that no firm, body corporate or other association shall be appointed as an inspector under Chapter XIV. The appointment of an inspector is of an individual. The section does not prevent a firm or body from assisting an appointed individual inspector.
content.glance: Inspector must be an individual — no firm, body corporate or association may be appointed as inspector; assistance by firms is not barred.
content.study: No firm, body corporate or other association shall be appointed as an inspector. Current-law framing: confirm that any person appointed as inspector under the investigation chapter is an individual; reject appointment of a firm or company as the inspector itself; note that professional assistance to an individual inspector is not prohibited by this section.

sections.heading: Prohibition
sections.body: No firm, body corporate or other association shall be appointed as an inspector.

sections.heading: Individual Appointment
sections.body: The statutory inspector is an individual competent person.

sections.heading: Assistance
sections.body: The section does not limit who may assist the inspector in a non-inspector capacity.

provisions.title: Firm, body corporate or association not to be appointed as inspector

examples.title: Firm named as inspector
examples.body: The Central Government proposes to appoint ‘XYZ & Co., Chartered Accountants’ as inspector. Section 215 bars appointment of a firm as inspector; an individual partner or other individual must be appointed.

examples.title: Assistance allowed
examples.body: An individual inspector engages a forensic accounting firm to assist. Section 215 does not prohibit such assistance; it only bars the firm from being the appointed inspector.

hypotheticals.question: May a company be appointed as inspector if it specialises in corporate investigations?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 215 expressly provides that no firm, body corporate or other association shall be appointed as an inspector. The appointee must be an individual.

distinctions.title: Who may be inspector (s. 215) vs appointment of inspectors (s. 210)
distinctions.left: Prohibition on firm/body corporate/association as inspector
distinctions.right: CG power to appoint one or more competent persons as inspectors

misconceptions.trap: Any professional firm can be named as the inspector under the Act.
misconceptions.correction: Section 215 prohibits appointment of a firm, body corporate or association as inspector. Only an individual may be appointed.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 215 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the proposed appointee. II. Apply the prohibition on firm/body/association. III. Confirm individual appointment. IV. Conclude.
